import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from collections import defaultdict

MAX_DRIVERS = 2

def design(feats):
    # Identify strong candidates based on t-statistics and effect sizes
    strong_candidates = []
    for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
        if feats.types[i] == 'clinical' or feats.types[i] == 'expression':
            t_stat = feats.x[:, i].std() * (feats.x[feats.y==1, i].mean() - feats.x[feats.y==0, i].mean()) / feats.x[:, i].std()
            effect_size = feats.x[feats.y==1, i].mean() - feats.x[feats.y==0, i].mean()
            if abs(t_stat) > 2.0 and abs(effect_size) > 0.1:
                strong_candidates.append((fid, abs(t_stat), abs(effect_size)))
    
    # Sort by t-statistic magnitude
    strong_candidates.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
    
    # Remove near-duplicates
    filtered_candidates = []
    seen = set()
    for fid, t, eff in strong_candidates:
        if any(abs(np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, feats.column(fid)], feats.x[:, feats.column(other_fid)])[0,1]) > 0.6 
                for other_fid in seen):
            continue
        filtered_candidates.append((fid, t, eff))
        seen.add(fid)
    
    # Select top candidates as drivers
    drivers = tuple(fid for fid, _, _ in filtered_candidates[:MAX_DRIVERS])
    
    # For logistic regression, include all features with significant associations
    columns = tuple(fid for fid, _, _ in filtered_candidates[:10])
    
    # Look for interaction terms between top candidates
    products = []
    for i, fid1 in enumerate(columns):
        for j, fid2 in enumerate(columns[i+1:], i+1):
            # Check if both features are in the data
            if fid1 in feats.ids and fid2 in feats.ids:
                # Compute correlation between products
                prod = feats.x[:, feats.column(fid1)] * feats.x[:, feats.column(fid2)]
                y_corr = np.abs(np.corrcoef(prod, feats.y)[0,1])
                if y_corr > 0.05:  # Threshold for inclusion
                    products.append((fid1, fid2))
    
    # Weighted score using top features
    loadings = {}
    for fid, _, _ in filtered_candidates[:5]:
        if fid in feats.ids:
            col_idx = feats.column(fid)
            # Use effect size as loading weight
            effect = feats.x[feats.y==1, col_idx].mean() - feats.x[feats.y==0, col_idx].mean()
            loadings[fid] = effect
    
    return Design(drivers=drivers, columns=columns, products=tuple(products), loadings=loadings)
